persona: Graduate research assistant in a rural health services program, digitizing a decade-old paper-derived clinic audit for a retrospective study of chronic-disease follow-up and hospital referral patterns in an underserved rural clinic; working directly from the original 2009 Excel file handed over by her faculty supervisor, who inherited it from the county health department field auditor who built it.
source_style: Legacy Excel 97-2003 (.xls) clinic audit workbook, originally compiled by a county health department field auditor in 2009 by re-keying a paper visit log; never reformatted or cleaned since.

columns.name: Patient_ID
columns.notes: Format 'CHC-00NN' for 38 of 40 rows. Rows 16 and 34 (physical rows) were re-keyed as bare numbers (15, 33) instead of the text ID -- a real re-entry slip, not synthetic noise for its own sake.

columns.name: Visit_Date
columns.notes: Real Excel date-typed cells (xlwt date format, MM/DD/YYYY display), all 40 rows populated. Range 2009-01-12 to 2009-06-08, weekdays only, matching the title band's stated Jan-Jun 2009 audit period.

columns.name: Age_Years
columns.notes: Integer age for 39 of 40 rows. Row 23 (physical) is the text 'approx 80' -- an elderly patient with no birth record, a common rural-clinic transcription pattern.

columns.name: Sex
columns.notes: 2 rows blank (sex not recorded at intake).

columns.name: Diagnosis_ICD9
columns.notes: 10 recurring ICD-9 codes (e.g. 401.9 hypertension, 250.00 diabetes, 466.0 acute bronchitis). 1 row blank, noted by the auditor as pending lab confirmation.

columns.name: Weight_kg
columns.notes: 3 rows blank (patient not weighed that visit).

columns.name: Chronic_Case
columns.notes: Real Excel boolean cells (xlwt/xlrd ctype 4, stored 0/1 under a boolean type tag), not TRUE/FALSE strings. All 40 rows populated: 9 True, 31 False. Set True for chronic diagnoses (hypertension, diabetes, asthma).

columns.name: Referred_Hospital
columns.notes: Real Excel boolean cells, same encoding as Chronic_Case. All 40 rows populated: 4 True, 36 False.

columns.name: Auditor_Notes
columns.notes: Mostly blank (29 of 40). Where present: administrative remarks. Row 27 (data index, physical row 29) carries 'Duplicate entry - retained per audit trail, do not delete' -- this is the hidden row.

clean_table.description: A correctly parsed table skips the merged title band (physical row 0) and reads physical row 1 as the header, physical rows 2-41 as the 40 data records -- including the HIDDEN physical row 29 (data record 27, patient CHC-0028), which is real data, not a formatting artifact, and must not be silently dropped just because Excel is hiding it from view. Patient_ID should coerce to a consistent text/string dtype (the two numeric-looking cells, 15 and 33, are the same kind of value as 'CHC-0015'/'CHC-0033', just missing the prefix -- they are not a different entity). Age_Years should coerce to numeric with 1 row unparseable ('approx 80', row 23) becoming a missing value rather than crashing the whole-column conversion. Chronic_Case and Referred_Hospital should be read as boolean dtype, not 0/1 integers or 'TRUE'/'FALSE' strings. Blank cells in Sex, Diagnosis_ICD9, Weight_kg and Auditor_Notes are missing data (NaN/null), not a valid empty-string category.

intended_analysis.primary_goal: Cross-tabulate Chronic_Case x Referred_Hospital (Fisher's exact test, given the small referral counts) to test whether patients with a chronic diagnosis were more likely to be referred to the county hospital.
intended_analysis.secondary: Descriptive summary of the visit cohort: age and weight distribution by sex, ICD-9 diagnosis frequency table, and visit volume over the Jan-Jun 2009 audit window.
intended_analysis.note: N is small (40) and the intended use here is testing whether a stats tool can even ingest the file correctly (dates, booleans, mixed-type ID column, the merged title band, the hidden duplicate row) before any inferential result can be trusted.

mess_applied: REQUIRED: genuine legacy .xls (BIFF, Excel 97-2003) written with xlwt -- confirmed openable by xlrd 2.0.2, which only reads the real .xls binary format.
REQUIRED: real date-typed cells in Visit_Date -- confirmed xlrd ctype==3 (XL_CELL_DATE) on all 40 data rows.

REQUIRED: real boolean-typed cells in Chronic_Case (and also Referred_Hospital) -- confirmed xlrd ctype==4 (XL_CELL_BOOLEAN) on all 40 data rows in both columns, written as Python True/False via xlwt.
REQUIRED: one merged title row above the header -- confirmed via sheet.merged_cells == [(0, 1, 0, 9)], spanning physical row 0 across all 9 columns.

REQUIRED: one hidden data row -- confirmed via sheet.rowinfo_map[29].hidden == 1 (physical row 29, i.e. data record 27), set with ws.row(29).hidden = 1. The hidden row is a real, fully-populated record (a duplicate visit entry the original auditor chose to hide rather than delete, per its own Auditor_Notes text), not a blank placeholder.

EXTRA (authentic, not required): Patient_ID mixed types -- 2 of 40 rows (physical rows 16 and 34) stored as numeric cells instead of the 'CHC-00NN' text pattern used elsewhere, a realistic re-keying slip.
EXTRA (authentic, not required): Age_Years has 1 text cell ('approx 80', physical row 23) among otherwise-integer cells, reflecting an elderly patient with no exact birth record.

EXTRA (authentic, not required): scattered missing values with no fill marker -- Sex (2 blank), Diagnosis_ICD9 (1 blank), Weight_kg (3 blank), Auditor_Notes (29 blank) -- ordinary not-recorded-at-intake gaps rather than a coded missing value.
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Reading physical row 0 (the merged title band) as either the header or as a data row, since a naive reader has no special handling for a merged cell sitting above the real header -- this misaligns every column.

Silently dropping the hidden row (physical row 29 / data record 27) if the reader filters on Excel's visible-rows-only view rather than reading every cell in the sheet -- this understates n from 40 to 39 without any error or warning.

Coercing Patient_ID entirely to numeric (turning the 38 'CHC-00NN' text cells into NaN and keeping only the 2 stray numeric ones), or the reverse -- treating the whole column as text and never noticing 2 of the 40 values are structurally different from the rest.
Coercing Age_Years to numeric and letting the single text cell ('approx 80') either crash the conversion for the whole column or silently vanish without being logged as a parse failure.

Treating Chronic_Case/Referred_Hospital as plain 0/1 integers rather than recognizing the underlying boolean cell type -- this changes how a tool would offer them for filtering/grouping (e.g. as a numeric variable to average instead of a binary group variable).

Treating a blank Sex/Diagnosis_ICD9/Weight_kg/Auditor_Notes cell as a valid empty-string category rather than as missing data, which would show up as a spurious extra level in any categorical summary.

Assuming Auditor_Notes is essentially unused because 29 of 40 cells are blank, and dropping the column -- which would also discard the only textual clue (on the hidden row) explaining why that record was hidden rather than deleted.

hidden_row_values: Duplicate entry - retained per audit trail, do not delete

_corrections: header_row 1 (0-based) -> 2 (1-based Excel row; title band is row 1, header is row 2).
